text:
sam: Nightly autopick CI flagged a regression when the autotuner picked the new candidate kernel on Ampere for long sequences (seqlen=2048). p50 ~same but p95/p99 up ~20-30% vs baseline. ticketing/logs: https://ci.redwood/tests/9282 :alarm_clock:

perf-ci-bot: nightly-run 2026-03-17T06:10Z finished. job=ci-autopick-ampere-2048 id=9282 artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/9282/summary.json

anika: thanks, linking artifacts. can someone paste the microbench stdout? want to see whether this is kv-cache related or kernel inner-loop difference.

lee: pasted below (ran locally reproducer from job 9282):
```
$ ./kbench --model=gpt-j --kernel=candidate_v3 --arch=ampere --seqlen=2048 --batch=1 --kvcache=enabled
kernel=candidate_v3 (sha=9f4b2a)
batch=1 seqlen=2048 tokens/sec=1200 p50=9.8ms p95=45.2ms p99=78.9ms
baseline (kernel=stable_v21) tokens/sec=1500 p50=9.6ms p95=36.1ms p99=59.8ms
regression: p99 +32%
```

zach: interesting — p50 is fine but tail blows up. smells like a slow path triggered by KV cache eviction or a path that only runs on long KV chain lengths. candidate_v3 added a different remat strategy and a new thread-local buffer for attention. could be memcopy or ATOMICS under contention.

anika: @zach can you try same microbench with `--kvcache=disabled` and also `--kvcache=warm` (2-step warm run) to see if warm cache hides it?

lee: did that quick:
```
--kvcache=disabled tokens/sec=1480 p99=60.2ms (close to baseline)
--kvcache=warm tokens/sec=1210 p99=79.5ms (same regressed tail)
```
So disabling kvcache removes the delta, but warm cache does not. points to behavior when KV depth >~1024?

sam: that lines up with the seqlen path selection: runtime picks a different attention kernel once keys > 1024. our autotuner recently exposed a candidate with better avg throughput but worse tail for large KV chains. we should gate this in CI.

anika: proposal: add a perf CI gate that checks p95 and p99 deltas on Ampere for seqlen=[1024,2048,4096]. block merge if p99 delta > 10% vs pinned baseline. Also add per-kernel telemetry (kernel_id, kernel_signature, fallback_reason) to nightly summary so we can correlate. I'll open a PR for both.

lee: question: how noisy is p99 in nightly? I'm worried about flakiness causing false positives. can we require 3-run median or use bootstrap?

perf-ci-bot: scheduled re-run: job=ci-autopick-ampere-2048-rerun id=9290 queued. will aggregate 3 runs and post median-based checks.

zach: also add microprobe that exercises long prefix rotations (random splits) — that often exposes atomic contention. if the kernel uses a global scratchpool we should measure contended memcopy latency.

anika: good call. i'll add an intrusive microprobe flag to the harness (kbench --probe=contention) so we can get per-call timings. will attach to nightly.

lee: quick triage idea: for now we can add an automatic fallback policy in runtime routing: if measured tail latency for candidate exceeds baseline by threshold on pilot nodes, route to stable. It's a cheap mitigation while PR gets fixed. who owns rollout config?

sam: infra does. @infra-bot can we flip a pilot fallback rule for model-family=gpt-j on ampere-pool for the candidate kernel sha=9f4b2a? fallback -> stable_v21 until resolved.

infra-bot: request received. created change: rollout-pilot-ampere-gptj candidate=9f4b2a fallback=stable_v21 scope=pilot. will activate after 15m if no objection.

lee: thanks. also adding a small reproducer that iterates over kv depths: 256,512,1024,2048 and logs kernel id and time per attention call. will push to the perf repo.

anika: opening a perf bug now: PERF-1147 "candidate_v3 p99 regression on Ampere long-kv paths". assigning to @zach, priority P1. attaching artifacts from 9282 and 9290.

zach: assigned and accepted. next steps: run perf with `--probe=contention`, inspect kernel assembly for memcopy loops, try patching to use per-stream scratch instead of global. will report back by EOD Friday.

sam: timeline sounds good. if we don't have a verified fix by Friday EOD, we keep the fallback active and block candidate from autotuner promotions.

perf-ci-bot: rerun 9290 completed. aggregated medians: p99_delta=+28% (ampere,2048). test_details: s3://perf-artifacts/9290/aggregate.json

infra-bot: FYI disk pressure on perf runners was moderate during the run, but logs indicate that the regression reproduces on a clean runner too. no infra issue blocking triage.

anika: created PR drafts: (1) ci-gate: enforce p99 delta threshold +3-run median, (2) telemetry: include kernel_id/signature in nightly summary. linking: https://git.redwood/infra/perf/pulls/412

lee: will review PRs. also will add a short doc in eng-runtime describing what to look for in seqlen-dependent regressions (kv depth histogram, memcopy hotspots, atomics).

sam: thanks team. summary: owner @zach, perf bug PERF-1147, mitigation=pilot fallback active, CI gate + telemetry PRs up, focused microprobe runs queued. keep updates in this thread and drop final EOD status. :thumbsup:
